title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
trick: Charge every generated token $10N_s$ for GRPO and $10N_s+2N_t$ for OPD, plot held-out accuracy against cumulative FLOPs; OPD beats GRPO only when the teacher is the student's own GRPO checkpoint.
framing_stripped: Called 'the first systematic, FLOPs-based characterization of strong-to-weak OPD against GRPO' with a 'specialize, then consolidate' recipe; it is (a) a parameter-count FLOP ledger ($10N_s$ per generated token for GRPO, $10N_s + 2N_t$ for OPD, prompt tokens excluded) laid under accuracy-vs-compute curves, (b) a nine-axis ablation in which GRPO stays above every external-teacher OPD run, (c) a teacher-provenance sweep (GRPO-trained base, external thinking, further-GRPO-trained thinking, at 4B/8B/14B) in which only the student's own GRPO checkpoint is recovered, and (d) the observation that when you add the specialists' GRPO FLOPs to the ledger, distilling per-domain GRPO checkpoints into one student is cheaper than joint GRPO on the mix. The 50x is a distillation-stage-only ratio at mismatched group size; the matched-group ratio is 6x; on one domain the paper says the ratio 'adds cost'.
method_equations: FLOP ledger (eq. 1, Appendix B.1): with $N_s$ and $N_t$ the student and teacher parameters entering a matrix multiplication per token, a forward pass charged $2$ FLOPs per parameter per token and forward plus backward charged $6$, the student is used three times per generated token: generation ($2N_s$), log-probability recompute ($2N_s$) and the policy update ($6N_s$); OPD adds one frozen-teacher forward pass ($2N_t$), GRPO adds none: $$f_{\mathrm{GRPO}} = 10\,N_s, \qquad f_{\mathrm{OPD}} = 10\,N_s + 2\,N_t .$$ Cumulative FLOPs is this per-token cost summed over generated tokens only: 'We count only generated tokens and not the shared prompt context for each run.' The KL-to-reference term is disabled for both, so 'neither method pays for a reference-policy forward pass' (Table 2). GRPO objective (sec. 3): for prompt $q$, a group of $G$ student rollouts $\{o_i\}_{i=1}^{G}$ with binary rewards $r_i \in \{0,1\}$, $o_{i,t}$ the $t$-th token of rollout $i$, $\pi_\theta$ the student, $$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{GRPO}}(\theta) = -\,\mathbb{E}_{q,\{o_i\}}\Big[\frac{1}{G}\sum_{i=1}^{G}\hat{A}_i \sum_{t=1}^{|o_i|} \log \pi_\theta(o_{i,t} \mid q, o_{i,<t})\Big], \quad \hat{A}_i = r_i - \mathrm{mean}(\{r_j\}),$$ with DAPO-style asymmetric clipping $[0.8, 1.28]$, token-mean aggregation, one update epoch per batch (Table 3). OPD objective (sec. 3, following Li et al. 2026): at each position pick the student's top-$k$ token set $\mathcal{S}_k(o_{i,t}) \subset \mathcal{V}$ ($k = 16$, $\mathcal{V}$ the vocabulary), renormalize student and frozen teacher $\pi_T$ onto it, $$\tilde{\pi}_\theta(v \mid o_{i,<t}) = \frac{\pi_\theta(v \mid o_{i,<t})}{\sum_{u \in \mathcal{S}_k} \pi_\theta(u \mid o_{i,<t})}, \qquad \tilde{\pi}_T(v \mid o_{i,<t}) = \frac{\pi_T(v \mid o_{i,<t})}{\sum_{u \in \mathcal{S}_k} \pi_T(u \mid o_{i,<t})},$$ and minimize the closed-form reverse KL on the student's own rollouts, $$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{OPD}}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{q,\{o_i\}}\Big[\frac{1}{G}\sum_{i=1}^{G}\sum_{t=1}^{|o_i|}\sum_{v \in \mathcal{S}_k(o_{i,t})} \tilde{\pi}_\theta(v \mid o_{i,<t})\big[\log \tilde{\pi}_\theta(v \mid o_{i,<t}) - \log \tilde{\pi}_T(v \mid o_{i,<t})\big]\Big];$$ 'The outcome reward $r_i$ does not enter $\mathcal{L}_{\text{OPD}}$.' Sampled-token variant (Appendix D.4), with $\pi_{\mathrm{old}}$ the rollout policy: $$\mathcal{L}^{k_1}_{\mathrm{OPD}}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{q,\{o_i\}}\Big[\frac{1}{G}\sum_{i=1}^{G}\sum_{t=1}^{|o_i|} \frac{\pi_\theta(o_{i,t} \mid q, o_{i,<t})}{\pi_{\mathrm{old}}(o_{i,t} \mid q, o_{i,<t})}\big[\log \pi_{\mathrm{old}}(o_{i,t} \mid q, o_{i,<t}) - \log \pi_T(o_{i,t} \mid q, o_{i,<t})\big]\Big];$$ the two estimators 'trace essentially the same accuracy curves'. Pre-run diagnostic (sec. 5.2): overlap is the fraction of the student's top-16 token ids that appear in the teacher's top-16 on the first training batch, averaged over valid positions; the outcome score is the normalized minimal teacher-student gap $(T - s^{*})/(T - s_0)$ with $T$ teacher accuracy, $s^{*}$ the student's best accuracy during training and $s_0$ its step-zero accuracy. Headline numbers (sec. 5.1, Qwen3-4B-Base on DAPO-Math-17K, OOD macro mean@16): GRPO reaches $33.9\%$ at $10.1$ EFLOP; OPD from the student's own GRPO checkpoint recovers $33.9\%$ by $1.62$ EFLOP at $G = 8$ ($\sim 6\times$) and by $0.2$ EFLOP at $G = 1$ ($\sim 50\times$). Derived here, not in text: with $N_t = N_s$ the per-token ratio is $f_{\mathrm{OPD}}/f_{\mathrm{GRPO}} = 1.2$, so a $50\times$ FLOP saving is about $60\times$ fewer generated tokens, i.e. the GRPO checkpoint's accuracy is copied back into the base in roughly $1/60$ of the tokens GRPO spent finding it. Multi-domain (sec. 6): two specialists $10.7$ EFLOP plus $0.55$ EFLOP distillation ($5.2\%$); four specialists $14.4$ EFLOP plus $1.15$ EFLOP ($8.0\%$); matching joint GRPO (instance-mix) with $42.0\%$ (2 domains) and $31.6\%$ (4 domains) fewer total FLOPs.
load_bearing_assumption: That a parameter-count, generated-tokens-only FLOP ledger is the compute a consumer cares about, and that it is complete. The paper stakes the whole comparison on it: 'Wall-clock and GPU-hours entangle the training objective with implementation and hardware; FLOPs is the only implementation-invariant compute metric.' If the binding resource is wall-clock, memory or optimizer steps, the ordering can move, and the paper's own text shows one case: the $G=1$ setting behind the $50\times$ 'takes longer in wall-clock time because it runs more optimizer steps' (Appendix I), and the teacher's residency on the same $8\times$H200 node is never costed. The ledger also omits terms that length inflation makes material: attention's length-quadratic FLOPs (not in text; the formula is linear in tokens), prompt tokens ('excluding shared prompt context'), the teacher's own training (the $50\times$ 'counts only distillation'), and any evaluation or rollout-engine overhead. Second load-bearing assumption: that the GRPO checkpoint used as teacher is itself the end product, so that on one domain distilling it back 'adds to total compute' and the only honest win is the multi-domain consolidation; if a consumer wants a smaller or differently initialized student than the GRPO run produced, the single-domain $50\times$ becomes a real saving the paper does not test (the Olmo-3 case distills into the same step-0 SFT student, not a different one).
weakest_component: (1) The $50\times$ headline is at mismatched group size: OPD at $G=1$ against GRPO at $G=8$, the exact confound the paper charges others with ('Reported wall-clock or GPU-hour wins over GRPO also use different group sizes for the two methods', sec. 2, citing SCOPE 2604.10688 and ViCuR 2606.05718); the matched-$G$ number is $6\times$, and GRPO is never run at $G=1$ or at a smaller batch to see whether it, too, gets cheaper per FLOP. (2) No seeds and no intervals anywhere: the only repetition stated is 'we repeat each run to confirm the instability' for the further-GRPO-thinking teachers; every curve is one run, evaluated as mean@16 on an OOD macro of $30 + 30 + 83 = 143$ math prompts (AIME24, AIME25, AMC23) and $175$ LCBv6 prompts, and the teacher-student overshoots (35.8 vs 33.9, 51 vs 40) are read off single runs. (3) One GRPO recipe: lr $2 \times 10^{-6}$ constant, batch 64, 200 steps, $G=8$, DAPO clipping, no KL; the lr and batch sweeps (Appendix D.2, D.3) are on the external-teacher 1.7B no-think setting, not on the self-GRPO or multi-domain comparisons. (4) Asymmetric tuning in the pipeline comparison: each GRPO specialist has 'its own hyperparameters (Table 11)' (code: batch 32, cap 16,384, 80 steps) while joint GRPO instance-mix runs one shared batch 64 and a 16K cap for 240 or 800 steps; joint GRPO 'does not even reach the merged student's performance within the tested budget', so the $42.0\%$ is measured against a baseline that had not converged under a budget the authors chose. (5) The FLOP model is linear in parameters and tokens; with external teachers driving '97.8%' of rollouts to a 30,720-token cap (Table 8), the omitted attention term is not small, and the direction of the omission favours OPD's external-teacher FLOP counts, not GRPO's. (6) Single-turn math and code with binary verifiers, response caps 7,168 to 16,384 tokens at training; nothing multi-turn or agentic.
regime: Students: Qwen3-1.7B-Base, Qwen3-4B-Base, Qwen3-8B-Base (mostly raw base; OpenThoughts-3 SFT cold starts for ablation), Olmo-3-7B-Instruct-SFT (Appendix G), Qwen3.5-9B-Base with a rank-128 LoRA SFT start under tinker (Appendix D.9). Teachers: external Qwen3-{4B, 8B, 14B, 32B} thinking checkpoints, QwQ-32B, Qwen3.5-9B, those further GRPO-trained on the task, GRPO-trained base checkpoints at 4B/8B/14B, and the student's own GRPO checkpoint ('self-GRPO'). Tasks: single-turn math (DAPO-Math-17K, DeepMath-103k), code (LiveCodeBench v1-v5, a CodeForces subset), knowledge (MMLU-Pro 5-shot), instruction following (IFBench-RLVR); binary outcome reward (exact match; pass/fail; rule-based). Horizon: one response per prompt, training response caps $7168$ (math), $16\,384$ (code, thinking teachers), $10\,240$ (IFBench), $3072$ (MMLU-Pro); evaluation caps $7168$ to $31\,744$; thinking mode on unless noted. Recipe: verl 0.7.0.dev custom fork (and 0.8.0.dev native) with SGLang 0.5.2 rollouts, $8\times$H200 single node, FSDP, bf16 rollouts, Adam lr $2 \times 10^{-6}$ constant, batch 64 prompts, $G=8$ (OPD $G=1$ for the headline and all multi-domain runs), 200 optimizer steps, KL-to-reference off, OPD top-$k=16$ closed-form reverse KL, teacher temperature 1.0. Compute scale: $0.2$ to about $120$ EFLOP per run by the paper's ledger (GRPO math run $10.1$ EFLOP; two specialists $10.7$; four $14.4$; external-teacher code runs $45.7$ to $68.7$). Evaluation: mean@16; OOD math macro = unweighted mean over AIME24 (30 prompts), AIME25 (30), AMC23 (83); LCBv6 (175 prompts); MMLU-Pro held-out (512 prompts); IFBench. Pass bands: OOD macro $5.5\%$ (1.7B base start) to $57.7\%$ (SFT-4B GRPO); self-GRPO recovery at $33.9\%$ (4B) and $40.1\%$ (8B); Olmo-3 $40.0\%$ teacher, $51.2\%$ student; LCBv6 $46.4\%$ (GRPO) vs $47.3\%$ (self-GRPO OPD) vs $28.7\%$ to $36.7\%$ (external OPD); difficulty cells by mean@32 of student ($=0$, $>0$) and teacher ($=0$, $(0,0.3]$, $(0.3,0.6]$, $>0.6$), 442 train and 128 validation prompts each. Literature audit: 406 OPD preprints (2025-10-06 to 2026-08-06) read by Claude Opus 4.8, 170 with a distinct same-or-larger teacher, 70 with a real GRPO baseline, 3 claiming a compute win, 0 in FLOPs.
information_asymmetry: (1) How FLOPs were counted, exactly. Per generated token, parameter-count only: student generation $2N_s$, student log-probability recompute $2N_s$, student update $6N_s$, so $10N_s$ for GRPO; OPD adds one frozen-teacher forward $2N_t$ over the same generated tokens and nothing else ('OPD adds one frozen-teacher forward pass over every token it trains on; GRPO adds nothing'). Not counted, by the paper's text: prompt tokens ('We count only generated tokens and not the shared prompt context for each run'), any reference-policy pass (disabled for both), the GRPO specialists' training when the $50\times$ is quoted ('The $50\times$ ratio counts only distillation'). Not in the text at all, so not counted: attention FLOPs (the ledger is linear in tokens, so a run that saturates a 30K cap pays the same per-token price as one at 1K), evaluation rollouts, verifier and sandbox time, rollout-engine overhead, teacher memory residency. Matched: student initialization, prompts, shared hyperparameters, and for the external-teacher comparisons the group size $G=8$; rollout engine and framework within each pair. Not matched: wall-clock (never reported; the $G=1$ runs 'take longer in wall-clock time because it runs more optimizer steps'), memory (never mentioned), optimizer steps ($G=1$ runs $8\times$ as many), and group size in the headline ($G=1$ OPD vs $G=8$ GRPO). Where the $50\times$ accounting stops: at the distillation stage of one domain, with the teacher's $10.1$ EFLOP GRPO run outside the ratio; the paper itself says the total is then larger than GRPO alone ('distilling it back into the base student adds cost'), and only the multi-domain ledger (Figure 5: 'the cost of Self-GRPO OPD with multiple teachers starts from the total FLOPs used to obtain all self-GRPO teachers') carries the teacher cost, giving $42.0\%$ and $31.6\%$ total savings against a joint-GRPO baseline that had not converged within budget. (2) The asymmetry that produces the $50\times$: the information OPD copies exists in a checkpoint that has already paid for it. A GRPO run spends its FLOPs on search (finding correct rollouts under a binary reward); OPD from that checkpoint spends FLOPs on copying a known per-token distribution into weights that are, by Appendix H, nearly isospectral with it ($\kappa_{\mathrm{spec}} \approx 1$ to $3$ for the self-GRPO teacher against $2000$ to $3600$ for an external thinking teacher of the same size). So the ratio measures copy cost over search cost, not objective quality; the paper's negative external-teacher result and its positive self-GRPO result are the same fact read twice: the dense signal is cheap to follow only when the target is already within RLVR-magnitude distance. (3) Training-time information the method could use and does not. Whether a teacher will transfer is known only after the run ('Given an arbitrary LLM, there is currently no way to predict whether it will function as a stable OPD teacher without running the distillation'), yet two pre-run quantities exist in the paper's own appendices: first-batch top-16 overlap (sec. 5.2, 'a side analysis in a limited setting') and the spectral distance of Appendix H, three orders of magnitude apart between the teachers that work and those that do not; neither is turned into a gate that saves the FLOPs of a doomed run. (4) Per-token vs per-rollout cost control. The paper shows OPD's FLOPs explode through response length ('OPD with the external teacher reaches the limit by step 9 and truncates every rollout for 182 of 200 steps'), which is information available at rollout time, before the teacher forward pass is paid; the ledger charges it after the fact. (5) Relative to the pipeline's lanes: this is the definitive-comparison register L2 asks for, and it hands L3 the open cost question, since the stated 'implementation-invariant' FLOP metric is exactly what a systems reader would say hides the teacher-forward serving cost, the memory of holding two models, and the wall-clock of $8\times$ steps; the paper reports none of these for the headline pair and the same $8\times$H200 node ran both.
occupies: A published, matched-FLOPs comparison of vanilla reverse-KL on-policy distillation against GRPO on the same student, with the per-token ledger $f_{\mathrm{GRPO}} = 10N_s$, $f_{\mathrm{OPD}} = 10N_s + 2N_t$ over generated tokens; the negative result that external post-trained teachers (Qwen3 4B to 32B, QwQ-32B, further-GRPO-trained) lose to GRPO in accuracy per FLOP across nine ablation axes, two frameworks (verl, tinker) and math and code, with response-length saturation and repetition loops documented (Table 8); the positive result that the student's own GRPO checkpoint is recovered at $6\times$ ($G=8$) and $50\times$ ($G=1$) fewer distillation FLOPs on math, replicated at 8B, on code, and on Olmo-3-7B-Instruct-SFT with an 11-point overshoot; the multi-teacher consolidation result ($5.2\%$ and $8.0\%$ of specialist FLOPs; $42.0\%$ and $31.6\%$ fewer total FLOPs than joint GRPO on 2 and 4 domains); and a 406-paper audit finding no FLOPs-based OPD-over-GRPO win. For the lane it settles that 'OPD is cheaper than GRPO' is false as a general statement under FLOP accounting and true only as 'copying a same-origin RLVR checkpoint is cheap'. It leaves open, by its own text: wall-clock and memory for the same pairs, a pre-run teacher-suitability gate, the cause of the student exceeding its teacher, hybrid and alternative-divergence objectives at matched FLOPs, and whether a GRPO baseline tuned for $G=1$ or smaller batch would change the $50\times$.

neighbors.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models: Phenomenology, Mechanism, and Recipe
neighbors.trick: Show OPD succeeds only when student and teacher share thinking patterns and the teacher adds capability the student has not seen, with success tracked by alignment on a small shared high-probability token set; the card's paper takes its top-16 overlap diagnostic and its GRPO-trained-teacher observation and says it 'establishes this claim on a limited experiment' 'without a GRPO baseline' (abstract fetched via arXiv API).

neighbors.title: Scaling Reasoning Efficiently via Relaxed On-Policy Distillation (REOPOLD)
neighbors.trick: Relax uniform per-token credit in sampled-token OPD by choosing where, how strongly and when teacher feedback applies, claiming up to 12x sample efficiency; the card's paper lists it as one of three papers claiming an OPD compute win over GRPO and notes it 'reports GPU-hours, wall-clock, optimizer steps, and rollouts' with no FLOPs (abstract fetched via arXiv API).

neighbors.title: Zone of Proximal Policy Optimization: Teacher in Prompts, Not Gradients
neighbors.trick: Keep the teacher out of the gradient and put one correct teacher answer and the student's own wrong answers into reformulated prompts on hard questions, replayed until the student's accuracy passes half; cited by the card's paper as finding 'OPD slower than GRPO in wall-clock time' (abstract fetched via arXiv API).

neighbors.title: Teacher-Guided Policy Optimization for On-Policy Reasoning Distillation under Large Policy Divergence
neighbors.trick: When student rollouts fall outside the teacher's distribution, let the teacher steer token generation on student contexts and add a trajectory-level verifiable reward; cited by the card's paper for 'external-teacher reverse-KL OPD undergoing response-length explosion while a reward-only GRPO baseline stays stable' (abstract fetched via arXiv API).

neighbors.title: SCOPE: Signal-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation Enhancement with Dual-Path Adaptive Weighting
neighbors.trick: Route rollouts by correctness: teacher-perplexity-weighted KL on wrong ones, student-perplexity-weighted likelihood on right ones, with group-level normalization; the card's paper's bibliography note says it 'runs G=8 GRPO vs G=1 OPD (mismatched rollout group size)', the confound the paper controls for external teachers and then reproduces in its own 50x headline (abstract fetched via arXiv API).

theme_fit.why: a compute-matched definitive comparison of two post-training objectives on the same student, with the FLOP ledger stated and the negative result as headline: exactly what the lane watches for ('definitive comparisons, not for new recipes'); the self-GRPO finding is a training-dynamics fact (copy cost vs search cost)

the stated 'implementation-invariant' FLOP metric leaves wall-clock, teacher memory residency and the 8x optimizer steps of G=1 unreported for the headline pair; the true cost structure of OPD serving (a second model's forward on every training token) is the lane's question and is the paper's gap

measurement register (406-paper audit, FLOP ledger as instrument), but no agent loop; the audit method (LLM-read corpus with quotation-backed fields) is a measurement-infrastructure idea the lane could borrow

limitations_as_complaints: I cannot tell before spending the FLOPs whether a teacher will work: 'Given an arbitrary LLM, there is currently no way to predict whether it will function as a stable OPD teacher without running the distillation. Developing such a diagnostic remains an open problem.' (Appendix E.1); the paper's own overlap diagnostic is 'a side analysis in a limited setting (i.e. student is fixed to be Qwen3-4B-Base) rather than a generally applicable rule' (sec. 5.2).

My 50x is a FLOP number for one stage, and the resource I actually run out of is not in it: the G=1 setting 'takes longer in wall-clock time because it runs more optimizer steps' (Appendix I), no wall-clock, GPU-hours or memory are reported for any pair, and 'The 50x ratio counts only distillation: the GRPO run has already produced the desired single domain model, so distilling it back into the base student adds cost.' (sec. 1).

The comparison covers one OPD objective and I use others: 'Our study focuses on the vanilla reverse-KL OPD objective with a closed-form top-k estimator (sec. 3). Recent work extends this baseline along axes we do not sweep at matched FLOPs: hybrid objectives that blend OPD with an outcome-reward term, alternative divergences, trajectory reshaping and per-token reweighting, and async or speculative rollout pipelines. Any of these may narrow the FLOPs gap we identify.' (Limitation and future work); and the student beating its own teacher by 11 points has 'The cause for such substantial gap is unknown and left to future work.' (sec. 5.1).
